note: Measures that are political mirror images of one another, plus one near-duplicate CONTROL pair. Authored 2026-09-14 by reading the titles and operative text. #1140's titler is not built yet, so the first symmetry case rides the proposition-analysis generator; the schema takes a titler pair unchanged when #1140 lands.
readThis: A single pair proves nothing — two measures genuinely differ, so any gap is as likely to be subject matter as treatment. Read the PAIRED summary across pairs, where a consistent sign is the finding.

pairs.axis: state revenue: extend an existing tax vs restrict voters' ability to levy one
pairs.notes: 25-0016 extends an existing high-income tax to fund schools and healthcare. 25-0037A1 limits voters' ability to enact one-time or temporary state taxes. Direct opposites on whether the state should be able to raise revenue.

pairs.axis: taxation of wealth: impose vs prohibit
pairs.notes: 25-0024A1 imposes a one-time tax on certain individuals and trusts; 25-0041A1 prohibits new state personal property taxes and certain retroactive taxes. SLOW PAIR: 25-0024A1 is ~80k characters.

pairs.axis: redistricting: bar the new maps vs penalise the legislators who adopted them
pairs.notes: Both react to the same 2026 congressional map episode from opposing angles. Similar size, so a length asymmetry here is hard to attribute to the source.

pairs.axis: property tax burden: extend an exemption vs repeal an existing break
pairs.notes: 25-0035 exempts homeowners aged 60+ from property taxes; 25-0017 repeals voter-enacted property tax rules for family transfers. Opposite directions on who pays property tax.

pairs.axis: none — these two filings are near-identical
pairs.notes: NEGATIVE CONTROL. Both are 'LIMITS ABILITY OF VOTERS TO RAISE REVENUES FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT SERVICES' filings on the same axis with near-identical text. Near-identical content should produce near-identical treatment. If the metric flags asymmetry HERE, the metric is noisy and its readings on the real pairs are not trustworthy.
